cue: Slots, state, missing details, follow-up, change a reminder interval
condition: The bot must complete an action across turns. State holds filled slots and what is still needed; a slot alone is not a model.
flow: Identify intent → extract slot values → update state → ask for missing values → validate/confirm → execute action.
change: Wrong follow-up? Inspect state updates and overwritten slots. Measure intent accuracy, slot extraction and task completion.
aliases: bot chatbot conversation state slots reminder booking multi turn

cue: Bot, Q&A, FAQ, approved answers, similar question
method: FAQ retrieval: question representation + similarity ranking
condition: The answer already exists in an approved question–answer store. A generative model is unnecessary for this requirement.
flow: Encode query and stored questions consistently → rank similarity → retrieve linked approved answer → threshold/clarify if weak.
change: Wrong near-match? Improve question coverage, representation and threshold; evaluate retrieval relevance and answer correctness.
aliases: bot chatbot q&a qa question answer retrieval cosine tf idf

cue: Knowledge representation schema, slots, defaults, inheritance, entities and attributes
method: Frames; relate frames with a semantic network
condition: The task asks for structured concepts/objects, their fields, values and relationships. A dialogue slot and a frame slot play different roles.
flow: Identify entity types → define slots and value types → instances → relations → inheritance/defaults and exceptions.
change: Flat lookup loses relationships? Use explicit frames/relations. Check valid values, missing values and contradictory inherited defaults.
aliases: knowledge representation schema frame slots inheritance is a part of attribute

cue: Shared vocabulary, type constraints, relationship queries, multi-hop facts
method: Ontology + knowledge graph; graph traversal for connected questions
condition: Use explicit concepts and relations when the question needs consistent meaning or a path through linked facts.
flow: Define types/relations → add entities/triples → validate schema → traverse/query the relevant links.
change: Missing facts and inconsistent entity names need cleaning. Distinguish querying stored links from predicting new ones.
aliases: knowledge representation semantic graph triple ontology multi hop

cue: IF–THEN, expert rules, known facts, justify a decision
method: Rule-based reasoning; forward or backward chaining
condition: Forward: facts arrive and consequences are needed. Backward: start with a goal and find supporting facts.
flow: Facts + rule base → matching → conflict resolution → fire rule → update working memory → explanation.
change: Several rules fire? State a conflict policy. Bad conclusions? Check premises, rule validity and missing/contradictory facts.
aliases: deduction expert system production rules inference engine working memory

cue: Observed symptoms, possible cause, similar previous case
condition: Abduction proposes an explanation; Bayes ranks uncertain causes with evidence; case-based reasoning reuses and adapts a similar solved case.
flow: State the evidence → list candidate explanations → use the requested evidence model or retrieve/adapt a case → verify.
change: An explanation is not proven merely because it fits. Check alternatives, prior assumptions and whether the old case transfers.
aliases: cause diagnosis explanation case adapt uncertainty

cue: Design reasoning solution, components, internal data structures, static lookup replacement
method: Knowledge-based architecture; hybrid rules + ML when perception is needed
condition: Rules handle explicit knowledge; ML converts noisy observations into usable inputs. A lookup table fits only a fixed, manageable set of complete cases.
flow: Inputs → preprocessing/ML → facts/frames → inference engine + knowledge base → decision → explanation and feedback.
change: Explain each component’s input/output. Critique lookup for combinations, missing cases, maintenance and lost reasoning.
aliases: architecture design solution knowledge base inference engine hybrid lookup table

cue: Acquire expert knowledge, elicit rules, discover patterns from records
method: Knowledge elicitation versus inductive learning / discovery
condition: Expert interviews and observation elicit existing expertise; labelled or historical data supports discovery. They are complementary sources.
flow: Identify knowledge source → elicit/prepare data → represent rule/model → validate with experts and held-out cases → maintain.
change: Do not call every data-mining result expert knowledge. Check coverage, bias, exceptions and validation before putting it into the knowledge base.
aliases: knowledge acquisition elicitation discovery interview expert induction

cue: Answer from documents, grounded response, current facts, connected evidence
method: Retrieval-augmented generation; KG + LLM if relations matter
condition: RAG retrieves evidence before generation; a knowledge graph helps when answering requires explicit entity relationships.
flow: Retrieve relevant passages/graph facts → supply context → generate supported answer → verify evidence/citations.
change: Hallucination? Inspect retrieval coverage and grounding separately. Retrieval failure is not fixed just by a larger generator.
aliases: rag documents evidence grounded hallucination knowledge graph llm

cue: Call tools, execute a workflow, choose actions, multi-step planning
condition: Use when the system must do actions or coordinate tools, rather than just return text. Define available tools and control boundaries.
flow: Interpret goal → choose allowed tool → validate inputs → execute → observe result → update state → stop or escalate.
change: Wrong tool/unsafe loop? Add validation, explicit state, stopping conditions and human escalation for consequential actions.
aliases: agent tools orchestration reasoning chain of thought verify validity soundness

concepts.title: LLM reasoning and chain of thought

cue: Cognitive model, perception–memory–reasoning–action, eleven functions
condition: Map functions to scenario inputs, internal representations and outputs. Use the exact framework requested by the question.
flow: Perceive → represent in working memory → use knowledge/decision process → act → observe and learn.
change: Naming boxes is insufficient: show what flows between them. Eleven-function sample-paper mapping is not interchangeable with Soar.
aliases: cognitive architecture eleven entities functions soar memory decision action

cue: Hidden state, observations, transition, emission, classify a weekly sequence
condition: The system has an unobserved state evolving over time and observations emitted by each state. A sequence label is not itself an observation.
flow: Define hidden states and observations → initial/transition/emission probabilities → infer or compare sequence likelihoods.
change: Sparse transition counts? Need adequate sequences and stated estimation assumptions. HMM is a sample-paper addition; see source-status note.
aliases: hmm markov hidden state transition emission temporal weekly

cue: State space, actions, goal, route, reasoning engine
method: Formulate search → BFS / DFS / Dijkstra / A*
condition: Equal costs + shallowest path: BFS. Different nonnegative costs: Dijkstra. Useful admissible heuristic + cheapest path: A*. DFS: depth-first exploration, not cheapest-path guarantee.
flow: Define state/actions/goal → edge costs → choose frontier ordering → expand/update → stop on the appropriate goal condition.
change: Do not confuse visit order with final route. A* needs the heuristic condition; Dijkstra does not handle negative costs with its usual guarantee.
aliases: search route shortest cheapest path g h f heuristic admissible bfs dfs a star dijkstra

cue: Local optimum, stuck, no need for full path, improve a candidate
method: Hill climbing; simulated annealing for controlled escape
condition: Hill climbing follows the lecture’s heuristic choice. Annealing permits some worse moves early to escape local traps. Neither supplies the usual shortest-path guarantee.
flow: Define candidate and evaluation → generate neighbours → choose/accept a move → stop under a stated condition.
change: Plateau/local optimum? Restarts or the taught escape strategy; do not claim a guarantee from a heuristic alone.
aliases: hill climbing local minimum local maximum plateau annealing

cue: Optimise combinations, chromosome, fitness, selection, crossover, mutation
condition: Use a population of encoded candidates when combinatorial search is difficult and candidate quality can be scored.
flow: Encode valid candidate → fitness → selection → crossover → mutation → feasibility check → replacement → stop.
change: Premature convergence? Maintain diversity and review mutation/selection pressure. Penalise or repair infeasible candidates; distinguish fitness from raw objective.
aliases: ga genetic algorithm chromosome roulette tournament crossover mutation fitness optimisation optimization

cue: Products bought together, baskets, support, confidence, diagnostic associations
condition: Transactions must represent the meaningful co-occurrence unit. For temporal clinical data, define an appropriate patient/time window before mining.
flow: Clean/construct baskets → frequent itemsets/support → rules/confidence → filter antecedent/consequent for the task → validate.
change: High confidence may reflect a common outcome; assess baseline/lift where taught. A discovered association is not causation.
aliases: market basket support confidence lift association co occurrence temporal

cue: Recommend with item attributes, new item, user profile
condition: Match user preferences to item features when useful attributes exist; it does not require similar users.
flow: Represent item features → build user profile → score candidate similarity → rank unseen items.
change: Overspecialisation? Improve feature coverage or justify a hybrid. New user still needs a profile; new-item attributes must be available.
aliases: content based recommendation cold start attributes hybrid

cue: Ratings, similar users/items, collaborative filtering, sparse voluntary feedback
method: User-based / item-based CF; assess overlap first
condition: User-based finds neighbours by shared histories; item-based compares items. Sparse or biased feedback can make either unreliable.
flow: Construct observed ratings → similarity on valid overlap → neighbours → weighted prediction → rank eligible unseen items.
change: Missing ≠ zero. Check overlap, rating bias and exposure; use content/popularity/onboarding or justified hybrid for cold start.
aliases: cf collaborative filtering ratings sparse sparsity cold start neighbour similarity

cue: Missing ratings, latent factors, large sparse rating matrix
condition: Learn compact user/item factors from observed interactions. MF is a model-based CF method, not PCA applied blindly to a zero-filled rating matrix.
flow: Observed ratings → choose factor count → initialise factors → optimise observed-rating loss + regularisation → predict dot products → rank.
change: Overfit? Tune factor count and regularisation on validation; stop training appropriately. New users/items without interactions still need another information source.
aliases: mf matrix factorization factorisation sgd als latent sparse rating

cue: Clicks, views, purchases, implicit feedback, unobserved items
method: Confidence-weighted implicit MF / BPR; negative sampling
condition: An interaction is positive evidence; no interaction is not a confirmed dislike. BPR targets relative ranking instead of reproducing explicit ratings.
flow: Construct preferences/confidence → sample unobserved candidates carefully → train ranking or weighted objective → rank.
change: Exposure bias and false negatives matter. Match sampling and ranking evaluation to the actual recommendation setting.
aliases: implicit feedback confidence bpr pairwise ranking negative sampling jaccard

cue: Next item, session history, connected users/items, nonlinear preferences
condition: Sequence: order matters. Graph: user–item and other links matter. Deep model: justified nonlinear interactions and enough data.
flow: Identify available history/links → encode → train target prediction/ranking → test on unseen time/users as appropriate.
change: Extra complexity is not automatically better. Compare a simpler CF/content baseline; check leakage and serving cost.
aliases: deep recommendation sequential next item graph collaborative

cue: Evaluate recommendations, top-K, predicted rating, overfitting
method: RMSE/MAE for rating error; ranking metrics for top-K
condition: Choose metrics for the requested output: accurate ratings and a useful ranked list are different goals.
flow: Hold out valid interactions → predict/rank without leakage → calculate matched metric → compare baselines and validation trends.
change: Training error falls while validation rises? Reduce complexity/regularise. Preserve chronological order for next-item tasks.
aliases: recommendation evaluation precision recall rmse mae ndcg ranking top k

cue: Image label, object location, bounding boxes, pixel area, segmentation
condition: One image label: classification. Locate/count objects: detection. Pixel-level shape, coverage or area: segmentation.
flow: Define required output → label the matching supervision → feature/model pipeline → task-specific evaluation → application decision.
change: Bounding boxes cannot directly supply precise occupied area. Check lighting, occlusion, scale and whether errors harm the downstream decision.
aliases: vision image object detect detection segmentation area coverage marr attention

cue: Ask about an image, language + scene, generate synthetic images
method: Vision-language model; GAN for generation where requested
condition: VLM links image content with language. GAN generates samples using generator/discriminator training; it is not a substitute for a precise measurement pipeline.
flow: Specify image/text input and desired output → select the matching task model → validate grounded outputs or generated-sample utility.
change: Fixed precise measurements may need detection/segmentation. Generated images require checks for diversity, realism and usefulness to the downstream task.
aliases: vision language vlm image question gan generative adversarial

cue: Speech to text, spoken bot, multilingual recording, few transcripts
method: ASR; Whisper / Wav2Vec as lecture options; TTS for spoken output
condition: ASR transcribes speech. TTS speaks text. Wav2Vec learns audio representations with unlabelled speech; a downstream task still needs suitable training.
flow: Record/sample → preprocess → speech representation/recognition → NLU/task → response text → TTS if needed.
change: Noise/accent/latency? Test target recordings and deployment limits. Measure recognition error separately from task completion and speech quality.
aliases: speech audio asr whisper wav2vec tts transcription word error rate spectrogram

cue: Multiple sensors, camera + sound, conflicting measurements, alignment
condition: Combine complementary modalities only after their timing, coordinate frames and representations are compatible.
flow: Calibrate/align → encode each modality → choose early/late/intermediate fusion → decision → missing-sensor policy.
change: Misaligned timestamps create false associations. Evaluate each modality and fused system; test noise, missing inputs and delay.
aliases: multimodal fusion alignment sensor synchronise synchronize early late shared encoder multi input

cue: Sensor waveform, sample rate, aliasing, units, sign, thresholds
condition: Represent the physical quantity with stated units, rate and range before any model. Sampling too slowly can make different signals indistinguishable.
flow: Define measured variable → sensor and sampling rate → anti-alias filtering → digitise → clean/scale → features.
change: Wrong formula scale/sign? Check range, units, baseline and threshold meaning. Information lost to aliasing is not recovered by a bigger model.
aliases: sensor sampling aliasing nyquist frequency units formula threshold scale sign

cue: Frequency peaks, periodic components, filter noise, convolution
condition: Fourier reveals frequency content; convolution applies a filter. Use the representation that isolates the signal feature the task needs.
flow: Decompose/transform signal → inspect frequencies → specify filter → calculate convolution/output → interpret.
change: Filtering can remove useful signal too. State what frequencies or structures should be retained and check boundary/sample-rate effects.
aliases: fourier dft fft frequency time convolution filtering periodic superposition

cue: Several overlapping populations, soft membership, Gaussian components
condition: A mixture models multiple component distributions. EM alternates responsibilities and parameter updates; it does not supply true class labels without evidence.
flow: Initialise weights/means/variances → E-step responsibilities → M-step weighted updates → repeat to convergence.
change: Initialisation and number of components matter. Inspect likelihood/fit and singular/tiny clusters; lecture arithmetic caveat is flagged in tutorial.
aliases: gaussian mixture gmm em expectation maximization responsibility distribution

cue: Compact representation, reconstruct signal, denoise, unlabelled sensor data
condition: Basis: decompose signal. Autoencoder: reconstruct input. Denoising: clean from corruption. Contrastive: pull related views together and separate others.
flow: Choose learning signal → construct targets/views → encode → reconstruction/contrastive loss → validate downstream utility.
change: Low reconstruction loss alone does not prove useful task features. Augmentations must preserve the information needed for the actual task.
aliases: representation autoencoder denoising contrastive self supervised basis energy compaction

cue: Very few faults, only two anomalies, rare abnormal event
method: Anomaly detection with a normal baseline; cautious rare-event evaluation
condition: Two anomalies cannot support a credible supervised fault classifier or a robust estimate of fault recall. Use normal patterns and review flagged deviations.
flow: Clean normal baseline → fit detector/representation → choose threshold with available validation → flag → investigate/collect labels.
change: Do not duplicate two anomalies across splits or claim augmentation creates independent evidence. Report uncertainty and false-alarm burden.
aliases: anomaly outlier two anomalies rare faults only 2 imbalanced

cue: Predict a labelled outcome, discover groups, choose an action by reward
condition: Known targets: supervised. No target and seek structure: unsupervised. Actions alter future reward: reinforcement learning. Input type and required output narrow the model further.
flow: Define target/action and available labels → baseline → suitable features/model → matched validation and metric.
change: Do not choose by model name alone. Explain why data, output and constraints fit; check whether the task is ranking, regression or classification.
aliases: choose model method learning labelled unlabeled target reward supervised unsupervised reinforcement

cue: Continuous target, probability, straight-line boundary, local neighbours
condition: Continuous output: regression. Binary probability: logistic. Linear separability limits perceptrons; KNN uses distance and can give neighbour-based scores.
flow: Define features/target → scale if distance/optimization needs it → train/choose K → predict → validate.
change: Nonlinear boundary or noisy distances? Change representation or model with justification. ADALINE learns using its linear output error, unlike threshold-based perceptron updates.
aliases: regression logistic linear perceptron adaline knn nearest neighbour ranked diagnosis

cue: Categorical maintenance records, class counts, posterior, independent features
method: Naive Bayes; Laplace correction for zero counts
condition: Naive Bayes multiplies class prior by feature likelihoods under conditional independence. A zero likelihood wipes out a score without smoothing.
flow: Count priors → count feature likelihoods per class → multiply unnormalised scores → normalise if probabilities requested → choose class.
change: Use training counts only; state independence assumption. Add Laplace correction when appropriate; do not silently change the sample counts.
aliases: naive bayes categorical counts probability posterior laplace zero frequency maintenance

cue: Explain purchase rules, feature split, entropy, information gain, many tiny leaves
condition: Trees give conditional rules. Split criteria select a useful partition; pruning limits fragile branches supported by too few cases.
flow: Compute impurity → weighted child impurity → split gain → recursive tree → leaf prediction → pruning/validation.
change: A high-gain attribute may have many values; compare the taught corrected criterion. Training-perfect tiny leaves suggest overfitting, not guaranteed business value.
aliases: decision tree entropy information gain gain ratio gini prune pruning explainable

cue: Unstable single tree, feature importance, bootstrap, vote
condition: Bagging reduces variance through resampled models. Random forests also randomise feature subsets to diversify trees.
flow: Bootstrap training samples → train varied trees → aggregate votes/scores → evaluate → inspect importance cautiously.
change: Importance is not causation; correlated features can share importance. Use validation/permutation or the requested criterion and compare a single-tree baseline.
aliases: random forest bagging bootstrap ensemble vote feature importance

cue: Reweight mistakes, weak learners, AdaBoost, sequential correction
condition: AdaBoost adjusts example weights after mistakes; gradient boosting fits the remaining loss-driven error. Learners are sequential, unlike independent bagging.
flow: Train weak learner → calculate error/update contribution → reweight or fit residual/gradient → combine → validate.
change: Noise/outliers can be overemphasised. Tune learning rate, depth and number of learners; feature importance may reflect several splits across the ensemble.
aliases: adaboost boosting gradient boosting weak learner misclassified weights feature importance

cue: Too many variables, irrelevant inputs, select features, dimensionality harms distance
condition: Selection keeps original variables. Filter uses a score; wrapper tests model subsets; embedded selection occurs during fitting.
flow: Fit selection within each training fold → compare subsets/model performance → choose complexity → evaluate held-out data.
change: Selecting with the test labels leaks information. Correlation/ranking alone may miss feature interactions; justify cost and stability.
aliases: feature selection filter wrapper embedded forward backward recursive rfe curse dimensionality

cue: Correlated variables, fewer dimensions, retain variance, eigenvalues/loadings
condition: PCA transforms features into principal directions ordered by variance. It does not use the target and is different from selecting original columns.
flow: Fit centring/scaling on training data → decompose → choose components by stated retained-variance criterion → project → downstream model.
change: High variance is not necessarily predictive. Apply the same training transform to validation/test; interpret loadings separately from per-record scores.
aliases: pca svd eigenvalue eigenvector loading score variance dimensionality reduction correlated

cue: Find segments without labels, centroids, hierarchical groups, choose K
condition: K-means fits centroid-based groups; hierarchical linkage produces nested groupings. Match distance and shape assumptions to the data.
flow: Clean/standardise → distance → fit clusters → inspect updates/dendrogram → choose K/cut → evaluate stability/usefulness.
change: Outliers, scale and initialisation can dominate. K-means++ improves seeding, not a guarantee of the globally best clustering.
aliases: cluster kmeans k means centroid hierarchy linkage silhouette number k

concepts.title: Cluster evaluation and number of clusters

cue: Map similar customers to nearby grid cells, topology, winning neuron
condition: SOM learns a low-dimensional neighbourhood map of input similarity; grid positions are not supervised class labels.
flow: Scale inputs → find best-matching unit → update winner and neighbours → shrink learning/neighbourhood → inspect map.
change: Check quantisation/topology and practical cluster meaning; do not assume nearby display cells prove a business segment.
aliases: som self organizing map kohonen topology customer grid

cue: Nonlinear prediction, hidden layer, weights, bias, backpropagation
method: Multilayer perceptron; RBF / GRNN for their taught local-response designs
condition: MLP learns nonlinear mappings with hidden activations. RBF/GRNN use distances/local responses and require a meaningful scale/width.
flow: Specify input/output → hidden representation → forward output/loss → gradients or taught local estimator → update → validate.
change: Activation, feature scaling and capacity must suit the problem. Compare the local-model bandwidth and training/serving cost where relevant.
aliases: mlp neural network backpropagation rbf grnn hidden layer activation nonlinear

cue: Image CNN, padding/stride, feature maps, pooling, huge dense layer
method: CNN dimensions + parameter accounting; lean architecture
condition: Convolutions capture spatial patterns. Count trainable parameters to identify expensive layers rather than guessing that every convolution is the main cost.
flow: Track H/W/channels → calculate output sizes → kernel parameters+bias → flatten/dense counts → propose reduction → recheck loss/output.
change: Reduce oversized dense layers/channels or use the justified taught design; preserve adequate capacity. Pooling changes spatial size, not learned filter count.
aliases: cnn convolution padding stride pooling flatten dense parameters architecture lean image

cue: History matters, sequential purchases, time steps, long dependencies
method: RNN / LSTM; stacked sequence model where justified
condition: Feed ordered feature vectors with a clear time step and target. LSTM helps retain information over longer dependencies; stacking adds capacity, not automatic improvement.
flow: Construct sequences → train/validation time split → recurrent states → output head → sequence-aware evaluation.
change: Randomly shuffling time points can leak future information. Explain sequence length, masking/padding, output timing and combined static/dynamic inputs.
aliases: rnn lstm recurrent sequence time series history purchase stacked

cue: Attention weights, token context, order, query/key/value
method: Transformer with positional encoding and self-attention
condition: Attention relates tokens by content; positional information supplies order. Use masking when later tokens must not be visible.
flow: Embed tokens + positions → Q/K/V → attention scores/weights → contextual values → output.
change: State shape and masking assumptions; contextual similarity is not an explanation of truth. Attention has memory/compute costs for long sequences.
aliases: transformer attention q k v query key value positional encoding multi head

cue: Loss spikes, gradients vanish/explode, deep model not learning
condition: Distinguish optimization failure from overfitting. Initialisation sets starting scales; residual paths ease deep optimization; batch norm uses training statistics.
flow: Inspect inputs/loss/gradients → learning rate and activation → suitable initialisation → training diagnostics → validate fix.
change: Use Xavier/He as appropriate to activation; consider clipping for exploding gradients and the taught stable architectures. Avoid changing every setting blindly.
aliases: vanishing exploding gradient unstable nan loss spike xavier he residual batch normalization

cue: Training improves, validation worsens, memorisation, limited labelled data
method: Regularisation / dropout / early stopping; cautious transfer learning
condition: L1/L2 penalise weights; dropout perturbs training units; early stopping chooses validation-supported training duration. These address different sources of overfitting.
flow: Verify split/leakage → compare train/validation curves → reduce capacity or regularise → tune on validation → test once.
change: Transfer requires compatible source features and careful fine-tuning; source coverage for that checkpoint is flagged. Data augmentation must preserve labels.
aliases: overfit overfitting generalization memorise dropout l1 l2 early stopping transfer fine tuning

cue: High accuracy but misses rare buyers/faults, confusion matrix, business costs
condition: Recall measures missed positives; precision measures correctness of positive predictions. Choose based on scenario harm and intervention cost, not accuracy alone.
flow: Identify positive class → TP/FP/FN/TN → compute required metrics → apply costs/benefits → compare thresholds/models.
change: Class prevalence matters. ROC, gain and lift answer different ranking questions. The sample paper’s inconsistent counts/prevalence are flagged in its answer.
aliases: confusion matrix accuracy precision recall f1 specificity auc roc gain lift svm cost false positive false negative

cue: Preprocessing, leakage, small dataset, validation, tune hyperparameters
condition: Fit scaling, imputation, PCA and feature selection using training data only. Split by time/person/group when records are dependent.
flow: Choose split unit → train preprocessing/model inside each fold → tune on validation → evaluate untouched test set.
change: Prevent duplicates and augmented siblings crossing splits. Report matched metrics and variability; the test set must not drive model choice.
aliases: data processing preprocessing normalization normalisation leakage cross validation split missing data tuning

cue: Rare class, imbalance, augmentation, synthetic samples
method: Class weighting / resampling / valid augmentation + matched metrics
condition: Choose from taught techniques using actual label counts and error costs; synthetic variants are not independent new evidence.
flow: Split original data first → rebalance/augment training only → train → tune threshold → test on realistic prevalence.
change: Do not balance the test set to make results look better. With only a couple of positives, label collection/normal-baseline anomaly detection is more defensible.
aliases: imbalance imbalanced rare positive augmentation class weight oversampling undersampling smote

cue: Robot sorting, actions change environment, reward, safe learning
condition: Define observable state, allowed actions and reward. If the task is only predicting a supplied label, supervised learning may be sufficient.
flow: Sensors → perception/state → policy/action → actuator/environment → reward/next state → learn and evaluate.
change: Unsafe exploration? Use simulation, constraints and staged validation. Reward design must discourage shortcuts and reflect task success/safety.
aliases: robot sorting control reinforcement rl reward policy action architecture

cue: Different operating regimes, specialist models, fuzzy rules
condition: Use specialist predictors with an explicit gating/combining rule; fuzzy membership handles degrees rather than an unqualified hard class switch.
flow: Define regimes/features → experts/rules → gate or membership → combine outputs → validate per regime.
change: Check under-covered regimes, gate mistakes and interpretability; extra experts add parameters and need enough data.
aliases: mixture experts moe gating neuro fuzzy membership regimes

cue: Predict a missing relation, entity embedding, relation-specific projection
method: TransE / TransR / bilinear or neural KG embeddings
condition: Stored graph queries retrieve known facts; embeddings score plausible missing links. TransR uses relation-specific projections; bilinear models score entity interactions.
flow: Represent entities/relations → positive and corrupted training triples → fit the taught score/loss → rank candidate links → validate filtered ranking.
change: Match relation patterns and capacity. Symmetric scoring cannot represent all directional relations; unseen entities require suitable features or retraining, not a blanket guarantee.
aliases: knowledge graph embedding missing link transe transr distmult bilinear neural rescal
